body:
[A10] Found in the #75 bench measurement (PR #604) by [R371] ([R371-2](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/604#issuecomment-5860551143) F5) and [R370] ([R370-2](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/604#issuecomment-5860541544)).

## Observation

On image `9e9954e9`, in 3 of 100 DUT-talker disconnect cycles (13, 24 and 75), the DUT's CRF talker kept transmitting through the 2 s unbound hold: about 1,000 PDUs, with no STREAM_STOP increment. The recorded tap data points to DUT-side behaviour:
- In the 97 cycles that did stop, the DUT's stream stops within one PDU period of the bridge's Listener withdrawal (`Lv`, 9.5-11.0 ms after the `DISCONNECT_RX` response; median stop 9.1 ms after the response). No ACMP DISCONNECT_TX appears on the tap, so the stop is driven by the Listener withdrawal.
- The MSRP profiles of the three non-stop cycles match those of restart cycles (13 and 75 match 42, 54, 59 and 90; 24 matches 36 and 80). So the bridge's `Lv` crossed the DUT's segment in those cycles too.

A talker that keeps streaming after its listener registration is withdrawn holds bandwidth and a reservation it should release.

## To do

1. Attribute from the retained per-cycle records of cycles 13, 24 and 75: when the bridge `Lv` and any Listener re-declaration crossed the tap, relative to the response and the continuing stream. PR #604 round 3 publishes those records.
2. Reproduce deterministically in simulation (the lwSRP talker path: Listener Ready withdrawn while the stream runs, including the race with a quick re-declaration) and find the state or timer that keeps the stream running.
3. Fix without weakening periodic refresh or LeaveAll recovery. On the bench, show that 100/100 disconnects stop the stream within one PDU period of the withdrawal, and that STREAM_STOP counts each stop.

Relates to #75 and #606 (the same lwSRP talker path). ALINX focus.
title: Talker keeps streaming after its listener withdraws (3 of 100 disconnects)
